title: Kestrel Enterprise - Assurance Trail and Evidence Manifest
summary: Working assurance trail for the Kestrel Enterprise POC. Collates artifacts we will hand to the customer's infosec team, maps them to SOC2/ISO controls, and records chain-of-custody/checksums for each file we plan to deliver. This is a living document used during the workshop and audit prep calls.
content:
Purpose:

Capture a compact, verifiable trail of evidence and decisions for the Kestrel Enterprise POC (dedicated / VPC deployment). This doc is the canonical working set for: audit packaging, live workshop notes, and the artifact manifest we hand to customers.

Scope:
- POC timebox: 2025-07-15 through 2025-09-30 (customer-run acceptance target: 2025-09-20)
- Components: control plane (Redwood private control plane in customer's VPC), serving nodes (dedicated GPUs), key management integration (customer KMS / optional HSM), network boundary docs, and observability traces for sample workloads.

Primary contact:
- Marisol Vega (solutions eng) — marisol@redwood.com
- Escalation: Aaron Kim (security lead) — aaron.kim@redwood.com

Executive notes from 2025-08-28 workshop:
- Customer asked for explicit artifact checksums with each deliverable (for chain-of-custody). We agreed to provide SHA256 digests and an exportable manifest CSV.
- Customer requests clear statement on whether logs containing PII will transit Redwood-hosted telemetry: our position is no telemetry leaves customer VPC unless specifically configured; default telemetry is metadata-only. Need explicit proof/config snapshot. (Action: Nikhil to produce telemetry config snapshot by 2025-09-02).
- HSM integration test passed in staging; customer requested HSM-backed sign/verify sample for key attestation (Action: Drew to generate sample signed artifact and include verification steps).

Evidence index (artifact file name -> short description):
- kestrel-architecture-v1.pdf — network and component diagram with VPC subnets, security groups, and peering notes.
- kestrel-kms-integration-screenshot.png — customer KMS console showing CMK created for POC.
- kestrel-hsm-attestation-sample.txt — sample signed nonce and verification steps.
- kestrel-access-matrix.csv — list of Redwood and customer principals used in POC with least-privilege notes.
- kestrel-deployment-manifest.json — automated deployment manifest (helm/kustomize) used for reproducibility.
- kestrel-eviction-and-fallback-tests.log — results from resilience tests showing fallback from dedicated to hosted variant.
- kestrel-observability-sample-traces.zip — 48h sample traces (scrubbed) showing token-level latency and cost breakdown.
- kestrel-sla-statement.md — agreed latency and uptime targets for POC (not contractual).

Controls mapping (top-level):
- SOC2 CC6 (logical access): evidence -> kestrel-access-matrix.csv, AWS IAM policies export (attached in s3 path), screenshots.
- SOC2 CC7 (configuration/change mgmt): evidence -> deployment-manifest.json, GitHub PRs (linked), release notes.
- ISO27001 A.10 (cryptography): evidence -> kms-integration screenshot, hsm-attestation-sample.txt, key rotation schedule documented.
- Network segmentation: evidence -> architecture pdf + VPC flow log sample (redacted).

Chain-of-custody process (how we produced the manifest):
1) Generate artifact from environment (logs exported with scrubber)
2) Store canonical artifact in s3://redwood-evidence/kestrel-poc/immutable/YYYYMMDD/
3) Calculate SHA256 digest and add to manifest (see checksum_manifest field below)
4) Produce human-readable manifest (CSV + PDF) and deliver via secure transfer (customer SFTP / signed URL with timebox)
5) Record transfer in audit log (jira:SEC-4821 comment + slack thread)

Workshop notes (live):
- 2025-08-28 10:15 — walkthrough of architecture; customer asked for example IAM policy that only permits model loading and inference (we will provide example policy: kestrel-inference-role.json).
- 2025-08-28 11:00 — telemetry/data-flow deep dive. Action: Nikhil to capture agent config -> telemetry_off_by_default.txt and provide a before/after sample.
- 2025-08-28 14:00 — HSM demo success; customer requested signed artifact + verification script (Drew).
- 2025-08-29 09:00 — packaging/transfer plan agreed: we will produce a single zip (kestrel-poc-evidence-20250901.zip) with manifest and checksums and provide a signed PGP of the manifest. Action: Evelyn to orchestrate packaging.

Open questions / risks:
- Can the customer accept our manifest PGP-signed or do they require an HSM-backed notarization? (ACTION: Marisol to confirm by 2025-09-03).
- Some telemetry artifacts still need redaction rules validated against customer DLP policy. (RISK: delays if DLP requires additional steps).
- Backup retention proof: customer asked to see backups-of-backups for config. We have snapshots for 90 days; need to export example snapshot to evidence bucket and attach. (Action: Aaron).

Delivery timeline (milestones):
- 2025-09-02: telemetry config snapshot + raw scrubbed sample
- 2025-09-04: HSM signed artifact + verification steps
- 2025-09-08: Final evidence zip assembled and checksums produced
- 2025-09-10: Customer review meeting, handoff via secure transfer

Notes on formatting & expectations (internal):
- Keep artifacts as small as practical; if full logs are requested, provide trimmed samples plus deterministic scripts to reproduce the export.
- All artifacts in s3 must be immutable (set object lock) and we must record the S3 object version ID in the manifest.
- Prefer PGP-signing of manifests and providing the public key thumbprint in the manifest for verification.

Appendix: sample manifest CSV header (what we'll provide)
- file_name,relative_path,size_bytes,sha256,sha256_signed_by,upload_timestamp,s3_version_id,notes

Appendix B: quick checklist for packaging (for Evelyn)
- [ ] collect final PR links and tag release
- [ ] run scrubber on observability exports (Nikhil)
- [ ] produce SHA256 checksums for each artifact (script: tools/checksum.sh)
